positioning.brief_for_strategy:
4 competitor(s) read - no open ground found.

**There is no open ground on the claims themselves.** Every axis this company competes on is claimed by somebody else too. That does not mean the email has to be generic - it means the difference has to come from specificity rather than from the claim: the one competitor carrying a real figure beats the four asserting the same thing without one.

**Contested - usable, but the reader has heard it.** Argue these, never assert them:
- **other** - Plausible added more new paying subscribers in April 2026 than in any other month in its seven-year history; April 2026 was Plausible's best month ever for new MRR and new customers; February 2026: 652 new paying subscribers; April 2026: 1,156 new paying subscribers; Plausible is used by 21,000+ teams (1 competitor(s) also claim it).

**Table stakes - true, and worth nothing as an argument.** Every competitor says these. An email that leads on one of them is an email the reader has already received:
- **price** - Trial signups increased 84% from January to April 2026 among non-logged-in visitors; Traffic increased by only about 2% from January to April 2026, even as trial signups rose 84%; The visitor-to-trial conversion rate rose from 2.65% in January to 4.80% in April; January 2026 trial signups: 2,423, register page conversion 38%, visitor-to-trial rate 2.65%; February 2026 trial signups: 2,656, register page conversion 48.8%, visitor-to-trial rate 3.09%; March 2026 trial signups: 3,608, register page conversion 52.8%, visitor-to-trial rate 3.64%; April 2026 trial signups: 4,464, register page conversion 57.3%, visitor-to-trial rate 4.80%; February 2026 set a new all-time record for trial signups despite being the shortest month of the year and having fewer visitors than January; February, March and April 2026 were three consecutive all-time records for trial signups in Plausible's history; From February through April, Plausible set new all-time records for both trial signups and new paying customers, three months running; Plausible's trial period is 30 days (4 competitor(s) also claim it).
- **breadth** - The Business plan supports up to 10 sites.; The Business plan supports up to 10 team members.; The Enterprise plan supports 10+ team members. (4 competitor(s) also claim it).

rivals.name: Google Analytics
rivals.why: It's the free default nearly every buyer already has installed, so switching means actively justifying leaving what GA4 already tracks

rivals.name: Fathom Analytics
rivals.why: The other paid, privacy-first, simple-dashboard tool a buyer puts in a side-by-side tab when they've already decided GA is out and just want the cleanest replacement

rivals.name: Simple Analytics
rivals.why: Comes up in the same 'no cookies, one dashboard' comparison as Plausible for buyers who want the minimal option and a rare free tier

rivals.name: Umami
rivals.why: The self-hosted, open-source near-clone buyers check when they want Plausible's exact feature set without paying a subscription

rivals.name: Matomo
rivals.why: Where a buyer lands when they want privacy-friendly analytics but also need heatmaps, funnels, and full data ownership beyond a single dashboard

rivals.name: PostHog
rivals.why: Where a team that outgrows simple pageview counting looks when they realize they also want session replay, feature flags, and product analytics in one tool
